answers.answer: Starting hands are 4 Player cards each for 2 players, 3 each for 3, and 2 each for 4. Remove and set aside Epidemic cards before dealing; shuffle the remaining City and Event cards and deal from them. Place each player's matching pawn in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove Epidemic cards; starting hands table; matching colored pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Flip 3 Infection cards and put 3 matching cubes on each city; flip 3 more for 2 cubes per city; flip 3 more for 1 cube per city. Put all nine revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the rest form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: marker on leftmost ‘2’; 3/2/1 cube groups; nine cards face up on discard pile; remaining cards form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic, removing unused Epidemics from the game. Split the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts, remove unused, equal-as-possible piles, one Epidemic per pile, smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; actions can be repeated and you may stop early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics first and discard or play Events until within the 7-card limit; then infect cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4, may repeat/stop; action discards to Player Discard Pile; draw 2 then infect; after all phases pass left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves along a white line to a connected city and costs no card. Direct Flight discards the City card naming the destination. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city you are in and moves to any city. Shuttle Flight requires being at a research station and moves to another city with a research station. White lines that go off one board edge wrap to the other (the summary gives Sydney–Los Angeles as an example).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Board wrapping edge case; Player Reference action costs.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a station from the supply, and place it in that city. If all 6 are built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions: Build a Research Station; Special Rules: research station limit and extras.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes 1 cube of one chosen color; because both cured colors are present, it instead removes all cubes of whichever one cured color is chosen from the city. It does not clear the other color or the uncured color in that action; each different color takes a separate action. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: cured disease returns all cubes of that one color; treat each different color with a separate action; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city's color need not match. Existing cubes remain, and the cured disease can still receive cubes from infections or Epidemics. If no cubes of that color are anywhere on the board when cured, it is immediately eradicated and its marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Discover a Cure action and Cure Procedure: station, matching-color cards, marker movement; existing cubes remain; no cubes means immediate eradication.

answers.answer: Normally, give or take the City card matching the city both players occupy. Both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge: matching current-city card, same city, both agree; recipient over 7 immediately discards or plays Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from their hand to a player in the same city, on either player's turn. The exception only transfers a card from the Researcher; another player cannot give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching card under this exception.
answers.evidence: Researcher role and Special Rules: may give any City card; on either player's turn; does not permit arbitrary nonmatching cards to be given to the Researcher.

answers.answer: After the actions, draw the top 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when a draw is needed, the game ends and players lose; discards are not reshuffled.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: top 2 together; fewer than 2 means loss and do not reshuffle discards.

answers.answer: Increase the Infection Rate first. Then draw the bottom Infection card. Since its city has 2 cubes of that color, add 1 to reach 3 and an outbreak occurs. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by shuffling only the Infection Discard Pile and putting it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game after resolving it; do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, bottom-card Infect, add only enough to reach 3 then outbreak, discard card, Intensify; no replacement Player card.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards per turn, respectively.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track table: positions 1–3 = 2, 4–5 = 3, 6–7 = 4; Player Reference maps Epidemics resolved 0–6 to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second; an Event may be played between them. Reduce an over-limit hand only after resolving any drawn Epidemics, discarding cards or playing Events until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once: resolve in sequence and Events may be played between; Hand Limit: first resolve drawn Epidemics, then reduce.

answers.answer: Flip the top Infection card, one at a time, for each card in the current infection rate. Normally place 1 cube of its color in its named city; if that disease is eradicated, place none. If the city already has 3 cubes of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. A cured but non-eradicated disease can still infect, so the normal placement/outbreak rules apply. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top cards at current rate, one cube, eradicated gets none, fourth triggers outbreak, discard each; Cure Procedure says cured diseases can still infect.

answers.answer: Resolve the current outbreak, then any chain outbreak in a connected city that already has 3 cubes. Advance the Outbreaks marker once for each outbreak. During chain reactions, do not add cubes to a city that has already had an outbreak while resolving that Infection card, so the spread does not place cubes back into the first outbreak city. Each color has its own cap of 3 cubes per city; cities may hold multiple colors.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker advances; chain reaction resolves after current outbreak; do not add cubes to cities already outbreaked this card; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. Once the Infection card has been drawn and its resolution is underway, Airlift cannot be played before that outbreak: Event cards cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card. After that card is resolved, an Event may be played before the next card is drawn/resolved. Airlift is not an action; the player playing it decides its use, and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player may play at any time, not an action, cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card, player decides use, discard to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Only 1 can be stored and it does not count toward the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Contingency Planner role: action, anywhere in Player Discard Pile, limit 1, stored on Role card, outside hand limit, remove from game on play.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own; moving another player's pawn requires the owner's agreement. Direct/Charter Flight discards come from the Dispatcher's hand, and a Charter card matches the moved pawn's departure city. When directing another pawn, the Dispatcher may move it but cannot make it Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role: two movement options, owner agreement, card payer and Charter departure city, no directed nonmovement actions, cannot use Operations Expert move.

answers.answer: The team wins immediately when cures for all 4 diseases have been discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. The three losses are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak), the supply lacks cubes needed for a placement (the loss occurs immediately during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection), or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions.
answers.evidence: Victory and Defeat: all 4 cures; three listed defeat triggers; cube supply check says immediate loss.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach and set 6 research stations and separated disease cubes nearby; place 1 research station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the 4 cure markers vial-side up near their indicators. Give each player a Reference card, shuffle Role cards and deal 1 face up to each, place the matching pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused Role cards and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the active player decides their actions. In Introductory play, all hands are face up; in Standard/Heroic, hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player decides; Special Rules: hand display by difficulty and discard-pile access.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of an uncured disease does not eradicate it. Removing the last cube of a cured disease does: flip its cure marker to the eradication side. Thereafter, no cubes of that disease are placed during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: uncured last cube has no effect; last cube of cured disease means eradication and flip; eradicated diseases get no new cubes during infections or Epidemics.

answers.answer: Place 3 cubes in the unprotected, non-eradicated city with zero cubes. Reaching exactly 3 does not itself cause an outbreak; the summary says an outbreak occurs if the city already has cubes and adding enough to reach 3 during the Epidemic, or if it already has 3 before an attempted placement. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Infect: place 3; if city already has cubes, add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard card. Outbreak definition requires already having 3 cubes for a normal placement.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. The eradicated disease receives no cubes. The bottom Infection card is still discarded to the Infection Discard Pile, and Intensify still reshuffles only that discard pile and places it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic steps always include Increase, Infect and Intensify; Infect says no cubes if eradicated and discard the card; Intensify reshuffles the discard pile.

answers.answer: After the first Epidemic's Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile, the second bottom Infection card is the only card shuffled by the second Intensify; it ends on top of the Infection Deck. The next normal Infection draws it first, normally causing an outbreak in that city (subject to effects such as an Event, eradication, or role protection).
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once: second bottom card is the only card shuffled on second Intensify, ends on top, and is drawn first in normal Infections, normally causing an outbreak subject to stated exceptions.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The action still requires being at a research station and the cards must match the disease color.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: 5 same-color cards, 4 for Scientist, at any research station; Scientist role repeats the 4-card requirement.

answers.answer: As an action, Operations Expert builds a research station in the city they currently occupy, with no City card needed, used, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert role: as an action, build in current city with no City card needed.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The card need not match a city; the special move starts at a research station and costs one action.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert role: once per turn as an action, move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.

answers.answer: The Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the city, including an uncured disease. It removes only that one color per action, not multiple colors together.
answers.evidence: Medic role: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color (not just 1).

answers.answer: When a cure is discovered while the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that color, remove those cubes there immediately, with no action stated as required. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another city with cubes of that cured disease via Dispatcher or Airlift on that player's turn, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that color from the city occupied or entered, also with no action needed.
answers.evidence: Medic role: automatic removal when cure is discovered in the Medic's current city; entry via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn triggers automatic removal; no action needed.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the city the Medic occupies. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic role: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's city, but not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents disease cube placement and outbreaks of every color in their current city and all connected cities. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role: all colors, current and connected cities; no effect on setup cubes.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any 1 card in the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between the Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded there before Intensify shuffles the pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Resilient Population removes any one Infection Discard Pile card from game and may be played between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: One Quiet Night skips next Infect Cities step and does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city. If it moves another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Airlift effect.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card hand limit. Role and Reference cards do not; the Contingency Planner's stored Event is on the Role card and does not count against the limit. A hand of nine must be reduced immediately to at most 7 by discarding cards or playing Event cards; after drawing, resolve any Epidemics first, then reduce the hand.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only, Role and Reference excluded, reduce by discarding or playing Events; resolve Epidemics first. Contingency Planner: stored card does not count against hand limit.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, whether or not the player is there, with no card discard needed.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Government Grant places a research station in any city with no card discard needed.

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put those cards back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: Forecast effect.
